license_provenance: HF dataset card YAML frontmatter `license: apache-2.0` at the pinned revision, corroborated by a real Apache License 2.0 LICENSE file in the project's code repository (github.com/Cohere-Labs-Community/MemoryCode, fetched and read: standard unmodified Apache-2.0 text). Not a badge. The card additionally names github.com/for-ai/MemoryCode as the project repo (the pre-rename org).

attribution.citation: From Tools to Teammates: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-Session Coding Interactions, arXiv:2502.13791

dataset.splits_note: one split only; there is no train/validation split to mis-select

verified_shape.method: counted from the shipped parquet at the pinned sha256; no card value trusted
verified_shape.history_regex_position: the last session of every instance, 360/360
verified_shape.schema_finding: `session_regex` / `session_eval_query` are NOT positionally parallel to `type` / `topic`: they align in only 811 of 8400 sessions. They are the cumulative ACTIVE-RULE set at that session (with one probe query per active rule), which is what the deterministic grader needs. `type` and `topic` do align 8400/8400. Anyone treating the four arrays as one parallel record will mis-pair rules to events.

label_provenance.verdict: synthetic-by-construction, and honestly described as such
label_provenance.evidence: The card's own first line: MemoryCode "is a synthetic multi-session dataset". No human-label claim is made anywhere, so there is nothing overstated. The load-bearing labels are the `session_regex` graders, which are hand-written rule templates, not model output: they are literal regexes (`['variable','^n_.*']`) and boolean predicates, evaluated deterministically.

verified_shape.grader: deterministic regex + boolean predicates in `session_regex`; NO LLM judge is required on any path

adapter.mode: retrieval-only, $0, no reader and no judge
adapter.unit: one session's `text`, ingested as a MemPhant episode (source_kind=user)
adapter.probe: a coding convention stated more than once across an instance's sessions
adapter.gold_rule: supersession groups are formed by stripping quoted literals from `topic` (`always start function names with 'a_'` and `... with 'y_'` collapse to one group). Gold = the session that most recently states the convention; distractor = every earlier session that states the superseded form. Uses only shipped fields; no model call.
adapter.probe_count_note: 1063 supersession groups across 257 instances, covering 3616 superseded (current, stale) pairs. 103 of 360 instances contribute no probe because no convention is restated in them.
adapter.metric: hit@1 / hit@k on the current session, plus `stale_outranks_current` -- the direct correction-retention failure mode

power.n_note: 1063 correction-retention probes over 257 instances; 3616 current-vs-stale pairs if scored pairwise.

resolvable_effect_size.paired_mcnemar_alpha_0.05_power_0.80: a 3.1pp absolute shift in hit@k (discordant-pair basis, assuming ~30% discordance)
resolvable_effect_size.unpaired_two_proportion_alpha_0.05_power: a ~6.0pp absolute difference between two independent arms at p~0.5
resolvable_effect_size.clustering_caveat: probes cluster in 257 instances (mean 4.1/instance); use a cluster bootstrap over instances. Cluster-adjusted, the resolvable paired effect is roughly 2x the flat figure, i.e. ~6pp.

power.why_this_closes_the_gap: The preference/user-learning lane currently has 51 never-scored goldens and no external instrument. This supplies 1063 externally-authored, deterministically-graded probes for exactly the construct that lane is about: a stated convention is later overwritten and the system must surface the current one, not the superseded one.

retrieval_only_full_run.note: local fastembed + local Postgres; no paid call on any path. Ingest bytes cover only the 257 probe-bearing instances; all 360 would be 21079968 bytes / 8400 sessions.

reader_ceiling_if_ever_funded.note: MemoryCode's native grade is regex. A reader would only be needed to generate code for the regex to grade, which is a separate experiment, not a cost of adopting the instrument.
